**The findings, and what was done.**
1. *Error.* The record's correspondence said that, under the split, P2 asks of a self that holds its effects only that its line continue at every alike step. Where the member conditions something and the class holds its effects, the condition keeps everything an alike occurrence conditions in the class (`«本类常闭则所缘同类»`), so it also forbids any alike occurrence to condition anything outside. Rewritten.
2. *Error.* "A member that conditions something" was dropped where idleness was stated: in the record's statement and second law, the root bullet, the README rows, the checker scope and §408. Where the member conditions nothing, a finer division can change the verdict (the reviewer's scratch witness). Restored throughout. The statement also now says where a line ends (at an occurrence that still conditions something), and that the split asks least where a predicate decides the class.
3. *Error.* The definition's docstring said the condition says nothing of how what lies outside is divided. It does: through "alike to it", for an effect that leaves the class (`FinerOutside`). Corrected.
4. *Error.* The reading said that finer divisions bear on which effects are one's own, P4's question. P4's predicate reads only one's own class, so they do not. The reading now says what they ask.
5. *Imprecise.* "Goes on" stood for "conditions something", but the glossary's "goes on" is 延, going on along some branch without end, and on finite nets the phrase was vacuous. Replaced in OC1's texts by "conditions anything" or "still conditions something", "alike step" by "alike occurrence".
6. *Imprecise.* The reading's last sentence holds only read with the split. It now says so, cites the sufficient condition (`«内外皆缘则二分本类常»`), and gives a witness where a finer division breaks it even there (`FinerWake`).
7. *Imprecise.* The reading set finer divisions aside because they do not bear on whether one's line ends before the net does. That criterion would also set aside the split's own clause on what leaves (`CleanStep`, read at the member's class). The reading now sets them aside because they ask one's effects to recur by kinds drawn in what lies outside oneself, and it says that even the split asks more than that one's line end where the net does.
8. *Imprecise.* P2's gloss, "whose line ends only where the net itself ends", is a consequence of the condition, not its content (`CleanStep.ends_where_net_ends`, `CleanStep.not_constant_at`). P2 now states the condition and gives the gloss as its consequence (`«亡而网续则本类不至终有常»`).
9. *Imprecise.* The conclusion stated under P2 alone what `«本类常闭则后皆续»` proves with P4 as well. Corrected.
10. *Imprecise.* `Inconstant` showed only the global failure. `Inconstant.not_constant_at` now shows it at the member's class, derived from `«本类常则闭当且仅当后皆同类»`, and the conclusion and P-20 cite it.
11. *Imprecise.* Step 2 and P-20's step 2 cited the organism's global failure; they now cite its failure at its own class.
12. *Imprecise.* The correspondence named in the record and in §408 covered half of the sufficient condition and left out the split. Restated in the record and in Boundary above.
13. *Imprecise.* The next step of what-leaves-a-class-follows-its-line said only P4's question remains. It now also says that reading P2 so is argued and that whether actual agents meet it is a correspondence.
14. *Imprecise.* §408's "it now holds as a law" overclaimed: the sufficient condition is a law of the split (`«内外皆缘则二分本类常»`), and that P2 passes a self drawn by intention rests on two readings, P2 read with the split and the class read as drawn by intention.
15. *Clarity.* "It bears on the condition only through 'alike to that effect'" cited nothing. It is now `«外分唯系出类之同»`, and `«闭则外分无关»` is its corollary.
16. *Clarity.* The witness bullets read as laws. They now describe their nets.
17. *Clarity.* What the removed Open item left (the reading argued, not proved; the correspondence) now closes the reading, linked to the record.
18. *Clarity.* `«闭则外分无关»` states one direction. "Gives the same verdict" applies it both ways, and the text says so.

**Corrections to §408.**
- Its Delta and "What it says" read "every alike step that goes on" where "every alike occurrence that conditions anything" is meant.
- "The division of what one leaves out matters only to a self that does not hold its effects" should read: it matters only where something an occurrence alike to oneself conditions leaves one's class, so never to a self that acts and holds its effects.
- "So P2 passes a self drawn by intention wherever …" holds read with the split (`«内外皆缘则二分本类常»`).
- "PF2 argued this from one witness; it now holds as a law" should read: PF2 showed one witness (`FiniteWake`); the sufficient condition is now a law of the split, and that P2 passes such a self rests on the two readings named in finding 14.
- Its Boundary's correspondence is restated in Boundary above.

**What it says.** P2 asks more than its gloss. A class whose every line from the member ends only where the net does can still fail it, where one alike occurrence leaves the class and another does not (`CleanStep`). Read at one's own class, what P2 asks of a self that acts and holds its effects does not depend on how what it leaves out is divided, since nothing leaves: every occurrence alike to it conditions only what is alike to it. For a self drawn by what it intends, the division of what it leaves out enters through what is alike to each effect that leaves, and only there (`«外分唯系出类之同»`). A finer division asks those effects to recur by kinds that the division draws in the rest, a regularity read off the rest's division, not off oneself. The split draws no kinds there. Read with it, P2 asks a regularity of one's own acts, of whether they stay or leave. It passes such a self wherever every alike occurrence that conditions anything both stays and leaves; under a finer division it can fail even there (`FinerWake`). That P2 is read so stays a labelled reading, and P4 stays the crux.

**PF's and PF2's wording.** The same use of "goes on" in PF's and PF2's texts (the module doc, the witness docstrings, 07 §4.6's home sections of PF and PF2 and its denial of P4, the root bullet, the checker scope and the README row) was replaced in this landing on the PF line owner's yes; no statement changed. Three kinds of use are kept, and OC2's board row names them. PF's two philosophy studies (`PHILOSOPHY-ROUND-1.md` and `PHILOSOPHY-ROUND-2.md` in `development/pf-path-and-crux/`) are cited by sha256 by PF's and PF2's records, so they stay as written. PF2's record keeps the use in its statement and third law, which were not on the list its owner answered; its home section already reads "every occurrence alike to the member that conditions anything". And "goes on past" an end (the module doc's first sentence, §4.6's step 2, D64's reading in §4.3, the record need-and-feeding-read-with-time, P-15 and P-20) means what `«过亡而续»` shows, a line that continues past an end, not one that goes on without end; it is left for a pass of its own over those texts.

**Constructivity.** No omniscience principle. `«外分唯系出类之同»` takes the case split as its hypothesis: each effect is alike to the member, or the two classes agree on what is alike to it. `«内外皆缘则二分本类常»` applies the backward direction of `«二分本类常当且仅当内外皆随»`, and the witnesses distinguish cases on their finite carriers. The receipt's empty axiom reports are the evidence.
